clue.text: Court official would be a valuable supporter ?

definitions.meaning: the royal household officer who carries a gilded rod at ceremonies
a precious metal gives value and a stick holds things up, so a rod of that metal is a costly prop

explanation.surface: Someone at the royal court is praised as a worthy ally.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold Stick is a title in the British royal household, held by an officer who attends the monarch on state occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a ceremonial officer of the royal court, and literally describes a precious rod that would prop something up.

clue.text: Sporting supporters of the bar

parts.note: the bar is the crossbar on a football pitch, held up by uprights at each end

explanation.surface: Fans of the pub who are good sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests fans and 'the bar' a pub or the legal profession; the bar is a crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: The uprights on a pitch that hold the crossbar up.

clue.text: Nobody's child makes a bloomer

definitions.meaning: the son of Mr Pooter in the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody
something that blooms, a garden flower

explanation.surface: An illegitimate child commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody (1892) is a British comic novel whose diarist Charles Pooter has a son named after a garden plant. 'bloomer' reads as 'blunder' but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The diarist's son in the novel, and a garden flower with tall spikes.

clue.text: Cynical, gives precious stone to coin collector

annotationWithheld.why: Cynical, gives precious stone to coin collector (8): SARD (precious stone) gives SARD, but no reading of 'coin collector' yields ONIC; the scan prints the same words, so the clue's second half cannot be parsed honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Cynical, gives precious stone to coin collector

clue.text: He follows new alto in opera

indicators.note: follows means the word He comes after the rearranged letters
new says the letters of alto and in are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man comes after a fresh alto singer in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the fodder and 'follows' places the pronoun last. The opera is by Gilbert and Sullivan, named after its fairy heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera about a fairy, named for its heroine.

clue.text: Captain of a steamer ?

parts.note: a fictional sea captain of adventure stories, whose name is also a steaming kitchen pot

explanation.surface: Who commands a steamship?
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kettle was the hero of popular Victorian sea stories by Cutcliffe Hyne, master of steamers; a kettle is also something that steams.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a fictional steamship master, and a pot that boils water and steams.

clue.text: County short of foreign money

definitions.meaning: the short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county
American dollars, informally, which are foreign to a British solver

explanation.surface: A county council finds itself without enough overseas cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckinghamshire, a county west of London, is commonly shortened; 'short of' reads as 'lacking' but 'short' means abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated county name equals the slang for dollars, currency from abroad.

clue.text: Go-between panted with redhead

annotationWithheld.why: Go-between panted with redhead (6): R (redhead) is clear, but the rest needs BROKE and 'panted' does not mean broke; the scan also prints 'panted', so the clue as held cannot be parsed honestly

clue.text: Someone admitting Edward, perhaps ?

definitions.meaning: a person who owns up or acknowledges a fault
Edward, the English king before the Norman Conquest, known by this title for his piety

explanation.surface: A person lets Edward in, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' reads as letting in, but it means confessing. Edward the Confessor was King of England 1042-66.
explanation.definitionFit: One who confesses is the title of a pious Anglo-Saxon king, Edward.

clue.text: Appears to understand the script

parts.note: to see is to understand
MS, manuscript, is a script

explanation.surface: Someone appears to follow what the text says.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the impression or look to be is a synonym.

clue.text: Dismay about unfinished red dress

indicators.note: about means the first word is put around the second

parts.note: to dismay someone is to appal them

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of red is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by a half-made red frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the D of 'red' and 'about' wraps the dismay word round what is left; 'dress' reads as a verb but is the noun for clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing and garments in general; dress used as a mass noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Beat the counter revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters of counter are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone defeats an uprising against the established revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges the seven letters of COUNTER; 'counter revolution' reads as one political phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat heavily or thrash an opponent is a synonym.

clue.text: Horse gets beer, perhaps — nothing more

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer, the 'perhaps' showing it is an example
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A horse is given a beer and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald or patchy-coated horse, especially in America, goes by this name.

clue.text: Sculptor takes no learners, East knows

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate, so two Ls are learners
E is the compass abbreviation for East
to ken is to know, in Scottish and old usage

explanation.surface: An artist refuses to take students, as the East knows.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Nollekens was an eighteenth-century London sculptor famous for portrait busts.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a Georgian English sculptor of busts.

clue.text: Neat end to a horse-race ?

definitions.meaning: of a drink, undiluted, served without water or mixer
the last stretch of the course with no bends, before the finishing post

explanation.surface: A tidy finish to a race at the track.
explanation.definitionFit: An undiluted spirit is served this way, and the run-in to the winning post is the home stretch of this name.

clue.text: Song cycle upset university

parts.note: a round is a cycle, a repeated circuit

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Yale is an American university

explanation.surface: A cycle of songs disturbed a university.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means read upwards, so the university's name is turned round. 'Song cycle' reads as one musical term but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A short simple song with a refrain, an old word for a lay or ballad.

clue.text: Mount is an animal none back

indicators.note: back means the pieces read together run in reverse order

parts.note: an ass, a donkey, is an animal
O is zero, none

explanation.surface: A mountain is said to be a beast with nothing behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ASS + O round. The mountain is in Greece, in the legend that giants piled it on Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek peak of legend, named as a specific mountain.

clue.text: Possibly tries to fill demands of stars

indicators.note: to fill means the rearranged letters go inside the word for demands

parts.note: asks means demands

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of tries may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps attempts are made to meet the demands of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the attempts to TERIS and 'to fill' puts that inside the demands. 'stars' means printed symbols, not celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Star-shaped printed marks, so called from the Greek for little star.

clue.text: A crab Len changed for another crustacean

indicators.note: changed says the letters of a crab and Len are put in another order

explanation.surface: A crab named Len was swapped for a different shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges A CRAB LEN; 'another' is fair because a crab is a crustacean too.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine crustacean that fixes itself to rocks and hulls.

clue.text: Warning successor?

parts.note: the siren signal sounded after an air raid alert, to say danger has passed

explanation.surface: Who takes over from a warning?
explanation.walkthrough: In wartime Britain, an air-raid warning siren was followed later by a steady signal meaning the danger was over.
explanation.definitionFit: The signal that danger is over, which comes after a raid alert.

clue.text: Course in which we have difficulty ?

definitions.meaning: a course of a meal, often the first
being 'in' this dish is an idiom for being in trouble

explanation.surface: A dinner course causes us trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is a British idiom for being in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter course at dinner, and the idiom of being stuck in it means trouble.

clue.text: Australian city retreat gives sailors about everything

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
about means the two sailors are placed around the word for everything

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
all means everything

explanation.surface: In an Australian city, sailors are retreating from something.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different sailors frame 'everything', and 'retreat' turns the whole run back to front. The city is a gold-rush town in Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold-rush town in the state of Victoria.

clue.text: He is engaged in cafe management

indicators.note: management means handling and arranging, so the letters of in and cafe are reorganised

explanation.surface: A man works in the running of a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' rearranges IN CAFE. 'engaged' reads as employed but means betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A man promised in marriage, betrothed.

clue.text: Type of emphasis ?

parts.note: type means typeface, and a sloping one is used to stress words

explanation.surface: What kind of stress is there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' reads as kind but means printing type: the sloping typeface is used for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanted printing typeface used to stress words.

clue.text: Where the feathers fly in Gloucestershire?

definitions.text: Where the feathers fly in Gloucestershire?

parts.words: Where the feathers fly in Gloucestershire?
parts.note: a shuttlecock is feathered, and the game took its name from a ducal estate in that county

explanation.surface: A place in a western English county where there is a fierce fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucestershire is a county in western England; the game played with a feathered shuttlecock is named after a great house there, also home to famous horse trials.
explanation.definitionFit: The racket sport using a feathered shuttlecock is named after a country house in Gloucestershire.

clue.text: Brooks nods ?

definitions.meaning: streams; a beck is a northern English stream
a beck is a beckoning gesture, a nod

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates nodding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooks' reads as the verb 'tolerates'; it means streams, a northern English word.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern streams, and summoning gestures such as a nod, as in 'at someone's beck and call'.

clue.text: Many a musical one in the game

definitions.text: Many a musical one in the game

parts.words: Many a musical one in the game
parts.note: the party game where players circle seats and grab one when the music stops

explanation.surface: Many a tuneful item features in the party game.
explanation.walkthrough: In musical chairs, children walk round seats while music plays and scramble to sit when it stops; there is always one seat too few.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat, of which there are many in the party game named after musical seats.

clue.text: Tree places third man by point

parts.note: Abel, after Adam and Cain, was the third man in Genesis
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tree positions the third man in cricket next to point.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man and point are cricket fielding positions, which the surface uses; here third man is the Bible's Abel, after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: The white poplar is a tree also known by this name.

clue.text: Officer has business with one in the fifties

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: in means the word one sits inside the pair of fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two Ls are fifties
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military man runs a company with someone in middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ONE between two Ls, the Roman numeral fifty doubled for 'fifties'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank, an officer above major.

clue.text: Mark the duplicity of his nom de plume

definitions.text: Mark the duplicity of his nom de plume

parts.words: Mark the duplicity of his nom de plume
parts.note: the pen-name Mark Twain contains twain, meaning two, so duplicity is doubleness; the clue asks for the writer's real surname

explanation.surface: Notice the deceit behind a writer's pen-name.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Langhorne was the author who wrote as Mark Twain; 'twain' means two, and 'duplicity' is used for twofoldness rather than deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: The real surname of the American author whose pen-name included the old word for two.

clue.text: Some dusty lecturer in fashion

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dull, dry lecturer appears in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in fashion' as the definition, but that is an adjective phrase and the answer is a noun; 'fashion' alone swaps for it and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A current mode of dress or design is a synonym.

clue.text: Gloomy admonition checks ovation?

definitions.meaning: a warning to an audience to applaud less, read as two words

explanation.surface: A dismal telling-off restrains the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words and it is an instruction to cheer less, which would curb an ovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal, without joy or comfort.
